title: 19.8 A 0.65V-VDD 10.4-to-11.8GHz Fractional-N Sampling PLL Achieving 73.8fsrms Jitter, -271.5dB FoMN, and -61 dBc in-Band Fractional Spur in 40nm CMOS
problem: Sub-0.7V ultra-low-voltage PLLs must achieve sub-100fs fractional-N performance, but existing DTC and DAC approaches face voltage-headroom limitations, nonlinearity, and noise folding at low supplies.
motivation: Digital-centric SoCs at sub-0.7V supply require low-jitter fractional-N PLLs for high-speed wireless transceivers, but voltage headroom constraints severely degrade phase noise and modulation performance.
method: LV fractional-N sampling PLL using coarse digital-to-time converter (LV-C-DTC) + fine resistor-based DAC (R-FDAC) with hybrid cascaded digital predistortion (HC-DPD) compensating nonlinearity of both DTC and sampling phase detector (SPD), plus negative-level-inverter (NL-INV) SPD reducing noise at low voltage.
key_novelty: HC-DPD technique reducing nonlinearity compensation overhead while minimizing noise folding; NL-INV SPD enabling low-voltage operation with improved voltage headroom.
contributions: Hybrid cascaded DPD reducing hardware overhead vs conventional DPD
Extended TSPC and TSPC multi-modulus divider supporting 10.4-11.8GHz operation
primary_theme: ultra-low-voltage fractional-N sampling PLL with smart predistortion
